text:
The Wild went into San Jose on Monday with headlines about Kirill Kaprizov chasing his own franchise record and came out with a 5-2 win. It was his fifth game of three or more points during a 15-game point streak, per NHL.com's Heather Rule. The team's run is 15 too: points in 15 straight (12-0-3).

The top line is the engine. Joel Eriksson Ek, Kaprizov and Matt Boldy have outscored opponents 26-2 at 5-on-5 with 61% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). Kaprizov has 24 points in his last 10 games against 15.1 expected, Boldy 18 on 11.3. Those numbers will cool, but the chances under them are real.

At 18-3-5, Minnesota's record runs about eight points ahead of its play by our standings model, and almost all of that is in net: the Wild have allowed about 16 fewer goals than their chances against predict. Take that away and they still have 56% of the expected goals, a contender's share.

Quinn Hughes gave them a scare last week, leaving the win in Calgary after a collision, but he has 16 points in his last 10 games, and his pair with Jared Spurgeon takes 65% of the chances. Brock Faber, settling back into the lineup, tied Monday's game late in the first period.

Our numbers make Minnesota a near-certain playoff team and give it 68% to win the Central. What we'd watch: the saves, because that is the only part of this that looks borrowed.
headline: Fifteen straight with points, and Kaprizov keeps climbing
